promotionRule: a requirement is verified only when the gate passed and a repository acceptance test named with its id passed; a decision is verified only when its evidence exists and every requirement it serves is so verified; invalid evidence is rejected; everything else is provisional

verified.statement: Suspensions are a Tier 1 Suspension record kept in Library.Suspensions (Map<MemberId, Suspension>); a member absent from the map is active. The Member record is unchanged so existing code and tests constructing members keep compiling.

The suspension check runs right after the member is found: in Loans.borrow and Holds.place after findMember (before copy/book lookup and all other rules); in Loans.renew after the loan is found, where the borrower becomes known, before the DEC-004 rules. Unknown member/copy/loan is still reported first. Returns are unchanged.
No renew command is added to the command line; the requirement's help list names only suspend, reinstate and member. The renewal block is enforced and tested in Tier 2 Loans.renew.
The JSON store gains an optional 'suspensions' array (member, reason, suspendedOn); stores without it load with all members active. The format tag stays 'lending/1' because the change is additive.
Help lists the three new commands directly after 'loans <member>' and before 'help'; README's command list is updated to match.

Days overdue are computed by Fines.daysLate(dueDate, today), the same function returnCopy uses for days late, so the overdue report and a return today always agree; a loan is overdue when that is above 0 (due today is not overdue); days are not capped, only the fine amount is.

Selection and ordering (days overdue descending, then copy id ordinal) are in Tier 2 Loans.overdue; Tier 3 Views.ofOverdue projects title and member name; the CLI only formats, including '1 day' versus 'N days'.
'overdue' is listed in help directly after 'member <member>' and before 'help'; extra words print 'usage: overdue' via the existing usage lookup; README's command list is updated.

'renew <copy>' calls a new UseCases.renew over the existing Tier 2 Loans.renew, so DEC-004's refusals, their order and existing error texts are reused unchanged. Loans.renew also applies the LEND-L01-R2 suspension check, so a suspended member's renewal prints 'error: member m1 is suspended'; this resolves the unit 1 open question about a missing renew command.
The limit in 'renewal N of M' comes from Tier 2 Policy.renewLimit via Views.ofRenew, so DEC-004's number is not duplicated.

LoanView gains Renewals; the CLI appends ' (renewed N)' only when N > 0, so never-renewed loans render as before. Renewals were already persisted, so the store format is unchanged. 'renew <copy>' is listed in help and README directly after 'return <copy>'.
The 5.00 threshold (Policy.maxOwedToBorrow, Tier 2) applies to every member type including staff; owing exactly 5.00 is allowed; refusal prints 'error: member m1 owes N.NN'.

What a member owes is the existing Fines.outstanding: the sum of all fines assessed under the schedule. Nothing pays or waives fines yet; DEC-006 waivers, when added, must be excluded from this sum. Store format unchanged.
'owes <member>' is listed in help and README directly after 'overdue'; the amount is formatted with the existing two-decimal Views.money.

Payments are applied to, and 'fines' lists, fines in Library.Fines list order, which is assessment order (oldest first): Loans.returnCopy appends each new fine and the JSON store keeps the order. The handoff note claiming newest first is false.

Fine gains Paid (0..Amount); Amount is never changed (DEC-006). Payments.pay fills the oldest fine first when the payment is made and also keeps a Payment (member, amount, day) in Library.Payments. Fines.outstanding (owes and the borrowing threshold) is the sum of Amount - Paid; this supersedes U4-D4's 'sum of all fines'.
The JSON store gains an optional 'paid' on each fine (missing = 0) and an optional 'payments' array (member, amount, paidOn); format tag stays 'lending/1' because the change is additive, as in U1-D6.
pay/fines output uses Views.money and Views.date; help and README list 'pay <member> <amount>' then 'fines <member>' directly after 'owes <member>'.

Fines.outstanding did not leave out waived fines (no waiver existed); it now sums the unpaid part of fines that are not waived (Fines.counts), so owes, the LEND-L04-R2 borrowing restriction and the pay limit exclude waived fines, and Payments allocation skips waived fines.

Fine gains Waiver: Waiver option (approver, waivedOn). Waiving never changes Amount or Paid (nothing refunded). The waived fine is the last fine in Library.Fines (oldest first) for the copy that is not yet waived, whichever member it belongs to.

Each fine is stored with an optional 'waiver' object (approver, waivedOn) or null; missing means not waived; format stays 'lending/1'. help and README list 'waive <copy> <approver>' directly after 'fines <member>'; fines lines append ', waived by <approver>'.

provisional.statement: The day of suspension (from the Clock port) is stored as Suspension.SuspendedOn for audit; it is not displayed.
An empty suspension reason is refused with 'error: a suspension needs a reason', after the unknown-member and already-suspended checks, following the existing name/title validation style.
LEND-L04-R3 is not implemented because Ordo reports ORDO.CONTRACT.UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT (CONFLICT-L04-STAFF-BORROWING) for it; staff borrowing keeps every existing rule.
In Loans.borrow the money-owed check runs right after the suspension check and before the copy lookup, loan limit and holds rules; the requirement does not dictate this order.

A valid amount matches digits with an optional point and one or two digits and is above 0 (signs, exponents, commas, '2.' and '.5' are invalid); Payments.parseAmount (Tier 2) is the only way to build a PaymentAmount. Refusal order: invalid amount, unknown member, payment above owed ('error: m1 owes only N.NN', including 0.00). Suspended members may pay.
Policy.branchManagers (Tier 2) holds DEC-006 revision 2's names; an approver must match one exactly (case-sensitive); Waivers.BranchManager has a private constructor and is built only from that list.
waive refusal order: unknown copy, then approver not a branch manager, then no fine to waive. Fines of suspended members may be waived.
